defiscan.summary: Aave V3 is a multi-pool overcollateralised lending market on Ethereum with four parallel deployments — Main, Lido, Prime/EtherFi, and Horizon RWA — each with its own Pool/PoolConfigurator/ACLManager triplet and a shared Aave Governance V3 root. Borrowers deposit collateral (ATokens) against which they take variable-rate debt (VariableDebtTokens), with valuations driven by Chainlink primary feeds and Aave-deployed CAPO adapters that bound liquid-staking and yield-bearing collateral ratios. text: score = 0.6 × the protocol node's own rating + 0.4 × the TVL-weighted mean (weight = tvl_30d_ma share) of the latest published score of every rated vault that deposits into it; with no rated vault the node rating stands alone (applied.k1 = 1). The band is read straight off the thresholds, without the dwell rule that smooths vault bands, so it can move on any day. A vault that deposits into more than one protocol node (every Morpho vault: the framework and the Blue instance) counts toward each. Vault scores are the published ones — their caps were computed against the node rating as of their own date, so after a node re-rate the two terms agree again at the next nightly. chain_id narrows the vault set only.

risklayer.summary: Aave V3 is the largest decentralized lending protocol by TVL (~$11.7B across 20+ chains) with six years of production history and zero confirmed direct exploits of core Pool bytecode. Audit depth is industry-leading (47+ reports through v3.7, $5M Immunefi bounty), and Governance V3 provides on-chain AAVE/stkAAVE voting with 1-day and 7-day executor timelocks. findings.title: Ethereum AaveOracle Source Not Verified on Etherscan
findings.description: Core price oracle at 0x54586bE62E3c3580375AE3723C145253060Ca0C2 on Ethereum has no verified source code on Etherscan. This contract feeds asset prices for borrows, liquidations, and health factors across the largest Aave V3 deployment. Without verified source, independent auditors cannot confirm Chainlink integration, access control, or absence of malicious logic.

findings.title: Arbitrum GHO Token (CCIP Bridged) Source Not Verified

GHO is Aave's native stablecoin with mint/burn semantics tied to cross-chain facilitators. Unverified bytecode prevents confirming mint authority, role configuration, and CCIP bridge integration on this deployment.

findings.title: Pool and PoolConfigurator Use Immutable-Admin Upgradeable Proxies
findings.description: Core Pool (0x87870…4E2) and PoolConfigurator (0x64b761…b27) on Ethereum deploy InitializableImmutableAdminUpgradeabilityProxy. The immutable admin is PoolAddressesProvider, which can call upgradeTo/upgradeToAndCall via setPoolImpl and setPoolConfiguratorImpl (onlyOwner). A malicious or compromised governance execution could replace Pool logic to drain funds or alter liquidation behavior.

findings.title: PoolAddressesProvider Owner Can Reconfigure Oracle, ACL, and Core Implementations
findings.description: PoolAddressesProvider.onlyOwner functions include setPoolImpl, setPoolConfiguratorImpl, setPriceOracle, setACLManager, setACLAdmin, setPriceOracleSentinel, and setPoolDataProvider. On Ethereum the owner is Executor L1 (timelocked governance path). These functions represent concentrated configuration power over lending parameters, price feeds, and role management.
